description: Customs officers who have come for a wanted passenger.

open: Captain {captain}, this is {group}. You're carrying {passenger}, who is wanted here. Hand them over and there's a reward in it. Keep them and it's harbouring.
{group} to Captain {captain}. We have a warrant for {passenger} and we know they're aboard. Make this easy.
Captain {captain}, cut your drives. {passenger} is wanted by {faction}. We can do this the short way, with a reward, or the long way, with a fine and a cell.
This is {group}. Your manifest says one thing and our informant says {passenger}. Our informant has been right before.
hand-over: {passenger} is in custody. A reward has gone to your account. {faction} thanks you for your cooperation.
Received. {passenger} didn't look surprised. They rarely do. The reward is on its way, captain.
Docking collar sealed, prisoner transferred. Fly safe, captain. You did the right thing, whatever {passenger} is shouting.
pay: I'll log it as a faulty transponder. {price}. Don't bring {passenger} through here again.
{price}, and I never saw you. My shift ends in an hour and I'd like it to end quietly.
Fine. {price} and the warrant gets lost in the filing. It happens more than you'd think.
outran: Stop that ship! It's no good, she's too quick for us. We have your registration, captain.
Pursuit called off. You're faster than us today. We'll be waiting at the stations.
They're pulling away. Log it, send the registration on, and let her go.
caught: Running only makes it worse, and you're not fast enough to make it work. Weapons free.
You won't outrun a customs cutter in that. All ships, disable that vessel.
Nice try. Now we do it the hard way.
fight: Harbouring a wanted person, and refusing a lawful order. Weapons free.
That's the wrong answer, captain. All ships, take them.
Then we'll come and get them ourselves.

description: Bounty hunters after a passenger with a price on them.

open: Captain {captain}, {group} here. You've got {passenger} aboard and there's a price on them. We'll share it with you. Or we take them off a wreck. Your choice.
Afternoon, captain. We're {group}. {passenger} is worth a lot to people who aren't you. Let's be sensible about this.
This is {group}. We've followed {passenger} across three systems and we're tired. Hand them over and we'll cut you in.
{group} calling. Nothing personal, captain. {passenger} has a price, and we collect prices.
hand-over: Pleasure doing business, captain. Your share's sent. {passenger} will be fine. Probably.
Transfer complete. {passenger} called you a few names on the way over. Your share is in your account.
That's how it's done. Your cut's been paid. If you ever want steady work, look for {group}.
outran: Fast ship. We'll find {passenger} again, captain. Everyone stops somewhere.
She's away. Fine. There'll be other ports, and we know them all.
Too quick for us today. Tell {passenger} we said hello.
caught: Nice try. Nobody outruns {group} in a ship like that. Guns out.
Running? We've chased faster. Open fire.
We hoped you'd say yes. We planned for no.
fight: Wrong answer. Take the ship, and try not to hurt the bounty.
Then we'll do it the expensive way. Your expense.
Have it your way, captain. Weapons free.
grudge: Captain {captain}. Remember {group}? We remember you. We brought friends this time.
{group} here. You cost us a bounty and two ships' worth of repairs. We've come to collect.
We said we'd find you, captain. Pay what you owe us for last time or we take it out of the hull.
pay: That covers the repairs. We're square, captain. For now.
{price}. Fine. We'll call it even, and we'll call it a lesson.
Credits received. Don't make us come looking for you again.

description: Creditors come to collect a passenger's debt.

open: Captain {captain}, {group}. Your passenger {passenger} owes us {price} and has missed every payment. Settle it for them, hand them over, or we settle it with your ship.
This is {group}. We're not pirates, captain. We're worse: we have paperwork. {passenger} owes {price}.
Good day, captain. {group} would like a word with {passenger} about {price} and some interest. A lot of interest.
{group} calling. {passenger} borrowed {price} and a great deal of patience. The patience has run out.
pay: Paid in full. {passenger}'s account is closed. Do tell them we'll be glad to lend again.
{price} received. A pleasure, captain. {passenger} is a free person, financially speaking.
That settles it. You're a generous friend, captain, or a foolish one.
hand-over: Thank you, captain. {passenger} will work it off. Here's a small finder's fee.
{passenger} is ours now, along with the debt. Your fee is sent. Mind you never borrow from us.
Sensible. {passenger} is coming quietly, more or less. A fee for your trouble.
outran: Interest is accruing, captain. Tell {passenger} it's accruing very fast.
Away you go. The debt doesn't go anywhere. It just grows.
Fine. We'll add the fuel to {passenger}'s account.
caught: Running from a debt never works, captain. We'll take it out of your hull.
We've repossessed faster ships than yours. Open fire.
That's a breach of contract. Weapons free.
fight: Then the debt passes to you, captain, and we're collecting.
We did ask nicely. Write that down.
grudge: Captain {captain}. {group}. You have outstanding charges with us for damage to our ships. {price}, or we repossess.
{group} again. You cost us a debtor and two ships. We have your name on file now.
We never forget an unpaid account, captain. Yours is overdue.

description: Another faction's agents, sent to stop a witness talking or bring someone back.

open: Captain {captain}. We act for {faction}. {passenger} has things to say that we'd rather weren't said. Give them to us and you'll be paid for your trouble.
This is {group}. {passenger} belongs with us, captain. Let's not make this a diplomatic matter.
Captain, I'm with {faction}. {passenger} is confused and frightened and wants to come home, whatever they've told you. We'll pay well.
{group} here. You don't know what {passenger} is mixed up in. We do. Hand them over and walk away richer.
hand-over: Thank you, captain. {faction} pays its debts. {passenger} will be looked after.
Received. Your payment is sent. You'll forget this conversation, I'm sure.
{passenger} is with us now. You'll find {faction} generous to its friends.
talk-yes: Hm. Perhaps we've been misinformed. Go on, captain. We'll say we lost you.
You make a fair point. {faction} can't afford the noise. Fly on.
Very well. But {passenger} should know that we let them go.
talk-no: That's a fine speech, captain. It changes nothing.
We're not here to debate. Decide.
Nice try. Now answer the question.
outran: Let them go. We know where they're going anyway.
She's too fast. Report it. Someone else will finish this.
caught: You can't outrun us in that. Disable the ship, and keep {passenger} alive.
Running tells us everything we need to know. Open fire.
fight: Then we'll take them. Don't say we didn't offer.

description: A congregation who want a runaway back.

group: the Brothers of the Long Gate
open: Captain {captain}, peace be with you. We are {group}. {passenger} has strayed from us, and we've come to bring them home.
This is {group}. You carry one of ours, captain. {passenger} took a vow. We'd like to remind them of it.
Captain, we mean no harm. {group} only wants {passenger} back among people who love them. And watch them closely.
{group} calls on you, captain. Give {passenger} back to the fold. We can offer prayers, and a donation to your fuel.
talk-yes: Perhaps they must find their own way back. We'll pray for {passenger}, and for you.
You speak kindly, captain. Go in peace. The gate will bring them home in its own time.
Very well. Tell {passenger} the door is open.
talk-no: You don't understand what you're carrying, captain.
We have heard that argument before. From {passenger}, in fact.
Kind words. But we've come a long way.
pay: A gift to the congregation. We accept, and we'll leave {passenger} to their road.
{price}. The Choir is grateful. Fly in peace.
Your offering is received. We'll pray {passenger} comes back of their own will.
outran: Let them go. The gate sees everything.
Too fast for us, and perhaps that's a sign.
Go, then. We'll be waiting at the next station, and the one after.
caught: Running from us? That's not what the faithful do. We're sorry for this.
Then we must stop you. Forgive us.
Hold them. Gently, if you can.
fight: Then we'll take them back by force, and pray for you after.
We hoped it wouldn't come to this.

description: Scavengers who've heard what a passenger carries.

open: Captain {captain}, word travels. Your passenger {passenger} has something in their luggage worth a lot. We'd like it, or a fair price for leaving it.
{group} here, captain. {passenger}'s bag. Hand it over or pay us not to look.
We're {group}, captain. Someone in the last bar talked about {passenger}'s case. Let's have it, or {price}.
{group} calling. We hear {passenger} is carrying something they shouldn't. We'll take it off your hands.
pay: {price}. You can keep the bag, captain. Smart choice.
Paid. We were never here, and {passenger}'s luggage is none of our business.
outran: She's faster than she looks. Never mind, there's always another.
Let her go. Not worth the fuel.
caught: Run? In that? Open fire, lads.
You don't outrun scavengers, captain. We live on the leftovers of people who tried.
fight: Have it your way. We'll pick it out of the wreck.
Lovely. We like it when they say no.
grudge: Remember {group}, captain? You made us look bad. We've brought friends and we're in a mood.
{group} again. You owe us for the ships. {price}, or your hull.
We don't forget, captain. Pay up, or we strip you for parts.
